definitions.explanation: Sleeves that extend to the wrist, or a garment with such sleeves. Often used as a modifier for shirts, sweaters, and other clothing.

examples.japanese: {長袖|ながそで}のシャツを{着|き}た。
examples.english: I put on a long-sleeved shirt.

examples.japanese: {日焼|ひや}け{防止|ぼうし}のために{長袖|ながそで}を{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: I chose long sleeves to prevent sunburn.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{半袖|はんそで}から{長袖|ながそで}に{衣替|ころもが}えする。
examples.english: When autumn comes, I switch from short sleeves to long sleeves.

notes:
{長袖|ながそで} refers to long sleeves or any garment with long sleeves. It is everyday vocabulary used when discussing clothing choices, especially related to weather or seasons.

WORD FORMATION:
{長|なが} (long) + {袖|そで} (sleeve). The same pattern applies to {半袖|はんそで} (short sleeves, literally "half sleeves").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長袖|ながそで}のシャツ: long-sleeved shirt
- {長袖|ながそで}を{着|き}る: to wear long sleeves
- {長袖|ながそで}Tシャツ: long-sleeved T-shirt

USAGE:
Often used without a following noun — {長袖|ながそで}を{着|き}る means "to wear something long-sleeved." Common in conversations about weather and seasonal wardrobe changes ({衣替|ころもが}え).

RELATED WORDS:
- {半袖|はんそで}: short sleeves (half sleeves)
- {七分袖|しちぶそで}: three-quarter sleeves
- {袖|そで}: sleeve
- {袖口|そでぐち}: cuff, sleeve opening
